newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Oct 1.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian dramatist GARNET WALCH, whose works included "Australia Felx", was born in 1843.
English social reformer ANNIE BESANT, who promoted birth control, was born in 1847.
British actor and entertainer STANLEY HOLLOWAY, who was Oscar-nominated for his 'ALFRED DOOLITTLE' in the film "My Fair Lady", was born in 1890.
Australian pioneer goldminer DORIS BOOTH, who prospected throughout Papua New Guinea in the 1920s, was born in 1895.
Russian/American pianist VLADIMIR HOROWITZ was born in 1904.
American actor WALTER MATTHAU, who won an Oscar for his part in "The Fortune Cookie", was born in 1920. He was a leading man on Broadway, and later in film productions of "The Odd Couple".
Australian academic DAME LEONIE KRAMER was born in 1924.

Former American President and peanut farmer JIMMY (JAMES EARL) CARTER was born in 1924. In 1976, he narrowly wrested the presidency from GERALD FORD. Features of his presidency were the return of the Panama Canal Zone to Panama and the Camp David Agreements for peace in the Middle East. He was defeated by RONALD REAGAN in 1980.
Irish actor and singer RICHARD HARRIS, whose most successful films were "The Guns Of Navarone" (1961), "Mutiny On The Bounty" (1962), "Camelot" (1967) and "The Wild Geese" (1978), was born in 1930.

British singer and actress JULIE ANDREWS (JULIA ELIZABETH WELLS) was born in 1935. Her very English accent made her ideal for casting in musicals with British parts. She received an Oscar for best actress in WALT DISNEY's production of "Mary Poppins" (1964), and appeared nude in the film "S.O.B" (1981) under the influence of second husband BLAKE EDWARDS.
American singer SCOTT McKENZIE, who had a big hit with "San Fransisco" (Be Sure To Wear Some Flowers In Your Hair) in 1967, was born in 1944.

American singer DONNY HATHAWAY, who sang several duets including the hit "Where Is The Love" (1972), was born in 1945. He died after jumping from the 15th floor of the New York Essex House Hotel on the 13th of January, 1979.
Australian actress KATE FITZPATRICK, whose films included "The Removalist" and "Goodbye Paradise", was born in 1947. On stage she starred in the "Rocky Horror Show".
** EVENTS **
1880 : The EDISON Lamp Works began operations in New
Jersey, to manufacture the first electric light bulbs.
1903 : European railways were linked with Russia.
1908 : The Model-T Ford built by HENRY FORD went on sale
for the first time. It was the first motor car with left-hand drive.
1918 : British officer T.E.LAWRENCE (LAWRENCE OF ARABIA)
and the Arab forces of EMIR FAISAL captured Damascus from the Turks.
1926 : Aviation history was made when veteran

long-distance pilot ALAN COBHAM landed his sea plane on the Thames River, following a record 28,000 mile (44,800 kilometre) round-trip to Australia. Thousands of people lined the banks of the river as COBHAM landed his De Havilland 50 biplane.
1931 : New traffic lights, installed at Oxford Street in
London, were reported to have sped up evening 'rush hour' traffic by 90 percent.
1935 : JOHN CURTIN was appointed leader of the Australian
Labor Party, and federal opposition leader.
1935 : Sport became compulsory in German schools.
1936 : The BBC began regular television broadcasts in
London.
1938 : German forces entered Sudetenland, once part of
Czechoslovakia, following the signing of the Munich Conference agreement.
1939 : Britain called up another 250,000 conscripts,
following the declaration of war against Germany.
1940 : Petrol rationing was imposed in Australia, during
World War II.
1946 : Twelve Nazis were sentenced to death at the

Nuremberg war crimes trial. Ten of the 12 were hanged 15 days later. HITLER's deputy MARTIN BORMANN was tried in his absence and was believed dead, while HERMANN GOERING took a cyanide pill on the day he was due to be hanged.
1947 : Actress RITA HAYWORTH filed for divorce from ORSON
WELLS.
1951 : The ANZ bank was formed in Australia, an
amalgamation of the Union Bank of Australia and the Bank of Australasia.
1953 : Scotland Yard Police used a television appeal for
the first time, in their hunt for a murder suspect.
1959 : The price of calls from public telephone booths in
Australia rose to fourpence.
1961 : The last steam train ran on the London Underground
system.
1969 : The sound barrier was broken by Concorde 001 for
the first time, during a test flight over France.
1974 : Australian Prime Minister GOUGH WHITLAM addressed
the United Nations in New York, the first Australian Head of Government to do so.
1974 : Britain's first McDonald's hamburger restaurant
opened in South London.
1977 : North Melbourne won the famous Victorian Football
League (VFL) grand final replay, defeating Collingwood 21.25-151 to 19.10-124. On the 24th of September, the teams had tied the final (North Melbourne 9.22-76 to Collingwood 10.16-76).
1982 : The West German parliament threw out Chancellor
SCHMIDT and elected HELMUT KOHL, the leader of the Christian Democrats, in his place.
1987 : Forty-eight year old surrogate grandmother PAT
ANTHONY gave birth to triplets for her daughter KAREN FERRIERA-JORGE in Johannesburg, South Africa.
1987 : An earthquake shook Los Angeles for 20 seconds,
killing seven people and injuring at least 100 others. The quake registered 6.1 on the Richter scale, and was felt 320 kilometres away in Las Vegas.
1988 : MIKHAIL GORBACHEV was appointed President of the
Soviet Union.
1989 : Pakistan rejoined the British Commonwealth
following an absence of 17 years.
